name: Emotion Regulation Questionnaire
time_window_text: We would like to ask you some questions about your emotional life, in particular, how you control (that is, regulate and manage) your emotions.

items.text: When I want to feel more positive emotion (such as joy or amusement), I change what I’m thinking about.
I keep my emotions to myself.
When I want to feel less negative emotion (such as sadness or anger), I change what I’m thinking about.
When I am feeling positive emotions, I am careful not to express them.
When I’m faced with a stressful situation, I make myself think about it in a way that helps me stay calm.
I control my emotions by not expressing them.
When I want to feel more positive emotion, I change the way I’m thinking about the situation.
I control my emotions by changing the way I think about the situation I’m in.
When I am feeling negative emotions, I make sure not to express them.
When I want to feel less negative emotion, I change the way I’m thinking about the situation.

cognitive_reappraisal.very_low: Your responses suggest very infrequent use of cognitive reappraisal â€” reframing how you think about situations to shift their emotional impact. Many people find that practising this strategy can be a helpful tool for navigating difficult experiences.
cognitive_reappraisal.low: Your responses indicate low use of cognitive reappraisal. Most people vary in how often they use this strategy, and it may be worth exploring whether it could be a useful resource for you.
cognitive_reappraisal.average: Your responses suggest an average use of cognitive reappraisal. Your responses fall within the typical range for most people.
cognitive_reappraisal.high: Your responses indicate frequent use of cognitive reappraisal. This is generally considered an adaptive way to manage emotions and suggests strong regulatory resources.
cognitive_reappraisal.very_high: Your responses suggest very frequent use of cognitive reappraisal. This is generally considered an adaptive strategy, and your responses suggest strong emotional regulation resources in this area.

expressive_suppression.very_low: Your responses suggest very infrequent suppression of emotional expression. Most people vary in how often they hold back their feelings, and your responses fall within the typical range of open expression.
expressive_suppression.low: Your responses indicate low use of expressive suppression. Most people experience this occasionally, and your responses fall within the typical range.
expressive_suppression.average: Your responses suggest an average level of expressive suppression. Your responses fall within the typical range for most people.
expressive_suppression.high: Your responses indicate frequent suppression of emotional expression. Many people find it helpful to monitor this pattern, as habitually holding back feelings can sometimes increase internal emotional load.
expressive_suppression.very_high: Your responses suggest very frequent suppression of emotional expression. This is worth paying attention to, as over-relying on suppression can sometimes make processing emotions more difficult over time.
